items.title: Chats that finish the job
items.text: Give a chat a folder on your computer, and work you ask for goes on until it's done: it runs commands, shows their output as it's written, and asks before it changes anything. A task started in the terminal, web, or desktop shows in the others, and any of them can stop it.

items.title: Qwen 3.5 is the new everyday pick
items.text: Toskar recommends Qwen 3.5 9B on most computers with 16 GB or more. On our long tasks it finished all three, where Qwen 2.5 7B finished at most one. Qwen 3.5 and gpt-oss now call tools reliably, so they can search, read files, and do tasks.

items.title: Toskar in your terminal and in VS Code
items.text: toskarctl chat chats in any terminal, and starts Toskar if it isn't running. The VS Code extension is on the Marketplace and Open VSX. Step-by-step guides cover Claude Code, Codex, and Continue on your own models.

items.title: The AI news and your briefing, on request
items.text: Ask any chat to read today's AI news or what your automations found, such as "what's in my briefing", in any of ten languages. It works in the car too. Each person hears only their own automations.

items.title: Places are looked up, not made up
items.text: A request such as "Find a cafe in downtown Juneau" is looked up on the web before the model answers, so the names and addresses are real ones.

items.title: New chats start with your default profile
items.text: New chats use General Assistant unless you pick another default on the Profiles page. A profile used once no longer carries over to every new chat, and profiles can't share a name.
